issues.claim: Westpac assesses assistance on a case by case basis, so the option offered depends on the customer's circumstances.
issues.evidence: Cited URL (now redirects to /help/support-with-tough-times/applying-for-financial-hardship-support/) does not say 'case by case'. Nearest wording: 'We'll work with you to understand your needs, circumstances and how an arrangement can help you get back on track.' The 'case by case' quote is on a different page, https://www.westpac.com.au/faq/type-of-assistance/: 'Assistance is determined on a case by case basis.'
issues.suggested_fix: Westpac says it will work with the customer to understand their needs, circumstances and how an arrangement can help them get back on track. (Or keep 'case by case' and cite https://www.westpac.com.au/faq/type-of-assistance/.)

notes: Cited URL redirects (HTTP 200, same content) to https://www.westpac.com.au/help/support-with-tough-times/applying-for-financial-hardship-support/. Update url metadata for this chunk and for hardship.westpac.apply and hardship.westpac.credit-report.

All claims supported (live page: 'Mon-Fri 8:30am-8:00pm, Sat 9:30am-6pm (Sydney time)'). Inconsistency elsewhere on the Westpac site: the deceased estates page lists Westpac Assist as '8.30am-7.30pm (Sydney time) Mon-Fri, or 9.30am-6pm Sat'.
Cited URL redirects to the applying-for-financial-hardship-support page.

issues.claim: free financial counselling is available through the National Debt Helpline.
issues.evidence: The Support for financial counsellors page does not mention the National Debt Helpline. It appears on the applying-for-financial-hardship-support page: 'The National Debt Helpline offers you free, independent advice from a Financial Counsellor... Contact them on 1800 007 007'. (Wrong source.)
issues.suggested_fix: Remove from this chunk, or cite https://www.westpac.com.au/help/support-with-tough-times/applying-for-financial-hardship-support/: 'The National Debt Helpline offers free, independent advice from a Financial Counsellor on 1800 007 007.'

notes: 'should give the counsellor permission' is implied by the page's required 'Signed Financial Counselling Agency Authorisation Form' or 'Authorised Third Party Form'; consider naming those forms and the email Financialcounsellors@westpac.com.au.

Missing nuance: the page says 'While the Customer Advocate does not review individual complaints, they work closely with their Westpac colleagues to provide support for complex and sensitive complaints.' The current wording ('not a channel...') is not wrong but omits that the Advocate supports complex and sensitive complaints.

The cited large-font guide is an older edition (footer '© 2021 ... WBCCCB003L 0921'); the live complaints page links a different, standard 'let-us-know-what-you-think.pdf'. NRS numbers are still consistent. The 'message Westpac within the Westpac App' claim was verified in the Personal Accounts T&Cs (effective 27 August 2026), as attributed.
'not originals' is not worded in the cited guide (it asks for certified copies). The deceased-estates web page states it explicitly: 'no originals as they may be destroyed'.

issues.claim: Westpac recognises three ways a trusted person can help with banking.
issues.evidence: The page lists seven authority types under 'Authorities at a glance': 'Authorised third party', 'Account signatory', 'Account sharing', 'Third party access', 'General power of attorney', 'Enduring power of attorney', 'Financial management order'.
issues.suggested_fix: Westpac lists several ways a trusted person can help with banking, including an authorised third party, an account signatory, account sharing, third-party access, a general or enduring power of attorney, and a financial management order.

issues.claim: An account signatory can operate the account, set up in a branch.
issues.evidence: Page: 'An account signatory is a trusted person you authorise to manage your account in branch.' Set up: 'Submit a Notice of authority (PDF 788KB) form in branch or add a signatory via Online Banking or in-app.' Access Levels: 'In-branch access only'. So setup is not limited to a branch; it is the access that is branch-only.
issues.suggested_fix: An account signatory can manage the account in branch (in-branch access only); the signatory can be added with a Notice of authority form in branch or through Online Banking or the Westpac App.

notes: Missing qualifiers on page: 'Exemptions for particular account types do apply' and the account is not unclaimed if 'you have notified us that you wish to treat the account as active'. The page also says customers can keep the account active with a transfer or deposit of at least $0.01.

issues.claim: Customers closing an account need to update anyone who pays into or debits the account and cancel periodical payments and direct debits.
issues.evidence: The close-account FAQ answer only lists the channels (Online Banking/App, branch, 132 032, +61 2 92939270). This sentence comes from the Personal Accounts T&Cs: 'It is your responsibility to notify anyone who either directly credits or debits your accounts (including ATO, Medicare and accountant/tax agent). Be sure to cancel any Periodical Payments, direct debits or credits...' (Wrong source.)
issues.suggested_fix: Attribute to the Personal Accounts Terms and Conditions (effective 27 August 2026): 'It is your responsibility to notify anyone who either directly credits or debits your accounts (including ATO, Medicare and accountant/tax agent).' Or remove it from this chunk.

notes: Missing condition: the page recommends reporting to ASD/ACSC 'If your fraud or scam case involves a payment activity'.

The SafeCall page itself gives the check: 'If you're not sure it's us, ask for a reference number, then hang up and call us back on 132 032.' Consider stating that instead of pointing to 'separate security guidance'.

issues.claim: A message or caller doing any of these is a warning sign of a scam, and it should be reported to Westpac through the Westpac App, Online Banking, or 1300 364 294.
issues.evidence: The online banking flyer (WL1766 05/25) doesn't give reporting channels. It gives 1300 364 294 only for case updates ('Want an update on your case? Visit westpac.com.au/scamcase or call us on 1300 364 294'). The reporting channels are on https://www.westpac.com.au/security/how-to-report/. (Wrong source.)
issues.suggested_fix: Remove the sentence, or cite the How to Report page: 'The fastest way to report a transaction is via the Westpac App or Online Banking... If you don't have access to Online Banking or our App call us on 1300 364 294.'

issues.claim: Westpac says the guarantee does not apply to Corporate Online Banking.
issues.evidence: The /security/ page's guarantee text doesn't mention Corporate Online Banking. The exclusion is on https://www.westpac.com.au/security/how-we-protect-you/ (westpac.com.au/protect redirects there): '* Our Online Banking Security Guarantee is not applicable to Corporate Online Banking.' (Wrong source.)
issues.suggested_fix: Keep the sentence but cite https://www.westpac.com.au/security/how-we-protect-you/ ('Our Online Banking Security Guarantee is not applicable to Corporate Online Banking'), or remove it from this chunk.

notes: The title promises 'lost or stolen card numbers', but the body has no phone number. Page: Emergency Card Services '1300 651 089 (or +61 2 9155 7700 if calling from overseas)'.

issues.claim: Westpac also says payments may take longer when paying a first-time payee or when a payment is caught for additional security screening, and paying someone for the first time usually requires a Security Code.
issues.evidence: The SaferPay page doesn't say this. It is on https://www.westpac.com.au/security/articles/creating-a-payee/: 'Payments may take longer in some instances, such as where there is a technical interruption to the service, there is a payment to a first time payee or when the payment is caught for additional security screening.' / 'When paying someone for the first time you will likely be asked to enter a Security Code.' (Wrong source.)
issues.suggested_fix: Cite https://www.westpac.com.au/security/articles/creating-a-payee/ for this sentence, or remove it. Possible SaferPay-only replacement: 'If we've categorised your payment as consistent with scam activity, the payment won't be processed.'

notes: The last sentence ('Time limits for other card types were not checked for this knowledge base') is an internal note, not customer-facing fact; consider removing.
'often called a credit ban' is a gloss not used in the Privacy Statement; harmless but not sourced.
